title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools Guide
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical Company Handbook page for Redwood Inference covering: what it means to work at Redwood, role definitions and career ladders, our benefits and perks, the hiring and new-hire onboarding process, and the primary internal tools every employee should know. The goal is to provide a single, readable reference for new and existing employees and managers.

1) Working at Redwood — our culture and expectations

Summary
- Mission-aligned: We prioritize shipping reliable inference infrastructure and developer-first tooling.
- Operational excellence: engineers own services through production; SLO-driven decision making is core to our day-to-day.
- Growth mindset: we invest in learning, feedback, and measurable career progress.

Core behaviors (what we expect from all employees)
- Own outcomes: prioritize customer-facing reliability, cost, and latency improvements.
- Communicate early: blockers, incidents, and cross-team dependencies.
- Ship iteratively: small, well-tested changes with clear rollback plans.

2) Roles & Career Ladders

Overview: Redwood uses leveled career ladders for Engineering, Product, and Design. Each ladder describes scope, impact, technical and leadership expectations. Managers use these for leveling, calibration, and promotion planning.

Engineer ladder (summary table)
| Level | Typical title | Scope | Example expectations |
|-------|---------------|-------|----------------------|
| IC1   | Software Engineer I | Task ownership within a single service | Delivers feature tickets, follows existing patterns |
| IC2   | Software Engineer II | Component ownership and mentoring | Designs modest features, owns on-call runbooks |
| IC3   | Senior Software Engineer | Cross-service impact | Leads design reviews, improves runtime perf 10-30% |
| IC4   | Staff Software Engineer | Architectural leadership | Owns major subsystems (serving runtime, kernel selection) |
| IC5+  | Principal/Distinguished | Company-level impact | Shapes product and infrastructure roadmap, represents Redwood externally |

Career guidance
- Promotions are evidence-based: concrete projects, metrics (latency, cost savings, reliability improvements), and peer/manager feedback.
- Annual calibration cycles occur in Q4; ad-hoc promotions possible for exceptional impact.
- Mentorship: managers and senior ICs are expected to provide regular feedback and 1:1 career plans.

3) Benefits & Perks

Core benefits (standard for all full-time employees)
- Health: medical, dental, and vision plans with employer-subsidized premiums.
- Retirement: 401(k) plan with company match up to 4%.
- Time off: flexible PTO (minimum 20 days/year), 12 company holidays, parental leave (primary & secondary), and caregiver leave.
- Family support: fertility benefits, adoption assistance.

Perks and development
- Learning stipend: annual $1,500 learning & conference allowance.
- Home office stipend: one-time $500 and quarterly $50 equipment reimbursement.
- Wellness: monthly wellness benefit and mental health coverage including 6 therapy sessions/year.
- Equity: new hires receive RSUs with standard 4-year vesting and 1-year cliff.

Benefits FAQ (selected)
1. Who is eligible? Full-time employees on regular payroll and approved contractors (after 6 months) for a subset of benefits.
2. How do I enroll? Use the People Ops portal (PeoplePortal) during new-hire onboarding or annual enrollment.
3. Parental leave policy summary
   - Primary caregiver: up to 18 weeks paid leave.
   - Secondary caregiver: up to 6 weeks paid leave.

4) Hiring & Onboarding Overview

Hiring process (high level)
1. Requisition & approval: Hiring manager submits req in Greenhouse with role profile and compensation range.
2. Sourcing & screening: TA screens and schedules initial recruiter screen.
3. Interview loop: role-specific loop (coding exercise for engineers, design exercise for product/design).
4. Calibration & offer: Hiring manager and interviewers provide feedback in Greenhouse; People Ops drafts offer and total comp.
5. Background check & hiring packet: offer contingent on background verification and signed agreements.

Interview guidance for interviewers
- Use the rubric in the Interviewer Guide: evaluate role-specific competencies, ownership, and culture add.
- Provide written feedback in Greenhouse within 48 hours.
- Avoid questions about protected characteristics; follow the inclusive interviewing checklist.

New-hire onboarding checklist (first 90 days)
Day 0
- Send welcome packet and equipment request via PeoplePortal.
- IT creates accounts: Okta, Google Workspace, Slack, Zoom, Jira, Confluence, PeoplePortal.

Week 1
1. People Ops orientation (HR basics, benefits enrollment).
2. Manager 1:1 to review role goals and 30/60/90 plan.
3. Team orientation: architecture tour, codebase overview, on-call expectations.

Month 1
- Complete security & compliance training.
- Shadow on-call rotations and runbook walkthroughs.
- Deliver first small project (bugfix or small feature).

Month 3
- Formal 90-day check-in with manager and People Ops.
- Identify development plan and mentoring pair.

5) Internal Tools and Guides (primary tooling every employee should know)

Account access matrix (who to contact for access)
| Tool | Purpose | Primary owner | Request flow |
|------|---------|---------------|--------------|
| Okta | SSO and identity | IT / Security | Auto-provision via PeoplePortal |
| PeoplePortal | HR, benefits, equipment | People Ops | People Ops team |
| Greenhouse | Recruiting | Talent Acquisition | Hiring manager/Talent |
| Jira | Tickets & planning | Eng Platform | Team admin |
| Confluence | Docs & handbooks | People Ops / Docs | Self-edit, request restrictions from Docs team |
| Slack | Real-time communication | IT | Self-join & channels |
| Internal Deploy Console | Deployments & rollouts | Eng Platform | Service owner approval |

Key internal guides (links and short descriptions)
- On-call runbook template — how-to for owning a service and handling incidents.
- Release checklist — preflight gating, smoke tests, canary rollout instructions.
- Security onboarding — required e-learning (phishing, data handling, RBAC).
- Cost & tagging guide — how to tag resources to attribute spend per product line and customer.

Common commands and snippets
- How to request access via PeoplePortal: PeoplePortal -> Access Requests -> choose tool -> add manager approval.
- Basic git workflow: git checkout -b feature/abc; git commit -m "feat: ..."; git push origin feature/abc; create PR using PR template.
- Deploy rollback: use Internal Deploy Console -> Select release -> Rollback -> add rollback reason and link to incident ticket.

6) Manager responsibilities and running effective 1:1s

Manager checklist (ongoing)
- Weekly 1:1s focused on priorities, blockers, career coaching.
- Quarterly goal setting aligned to team roadmap and company OKRs.
- Ensure direct reports complete required training (security, compliance, on-call).
- Ownership of performance reviews and promotion recommendations.

1:1 structure suggestion
1. Quick personal check-in (5 mins)
2. Wins, blockers, and priorities (15 mins)
3. Career & development discussion (10 mins)
4. Action items and follow-ups (5 mins)

7) Ownership, review cadence, and change log

Document ownership
- Primary owner: People Ops (Ava Chen)
- Reviewers: TA, Eng Platform, Security, Finance as listed above.

Review cadence
- Quarterly review for benefits and hiring sections.
- Bi-annual review for career ladders and role expectations.
- Ad-hoc updates for legal or compliance-driven changes.
